name: Sempra

profile.description: Sempra is a California-based energy infrastructure holding company operating regulated utilities SDG&E and SoCalGas in Southern California, a majority stake in Oncor (Texas transmission and distribution), and Sempra Infrastructure (LNG and energy networks). FY2025 revenue was $13.7B with net income of $1.84B. In 2026 Sempra affirmed adjusted EPS guidance of $4.80-$5.30, 2027 EPS guidance of $5.10-$5.70, and a 7-9% long-term EPS growth rate, while advancing the sale of a 45% stake in Sempra Infrastructure Partners to KKR to sharpen its focus on regulated utilities. Q3 2026 results are scheduled for November 5, 2026.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Sempra's last five years are defined by portfolio reshaping rather than new products: revenue moved from $11.4B in FY2020 to $13.7B in FY2025 (3.9% CAGR), and 2026 revenue is flat (-0.1% YoY) with Q2 2026 revenue of $3.0B missing consensus [1][2][3]. The pending KKR sale of a 45% Sempra Infrastructure Partners stake is a capital-structure move, not an innovation pivot [2]. AI Deployment (1/2): The utilities use AI-enabled weather forecasting and grid/wildfire monitoring operationally, but no quantified savings or AI products are disclosed [6]. Market Share (2/2): Sempra holds monopoly franchises through SDG&E and SoCalGas and owns ~80% of Oncor, the largest T&D utility in Texas [1][6]. Pipeline (2/2): A named multi-year capital plan with specific projects, including Oncor grid buildout for ERCOT large-load growth and Port Arthur LNG, underpins 2026-2027 EPS guidance of $4.80-$5.30 and $5.10-$5.70 [2][3]. R&D Intensity (0/1): FMP reports no R&D expense line, consistent with regulated-utility norms rather than top-quartile investment [4].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Sempra's purpose of 'delivering energy with purpose' and building North America's premier energy infrastructure is clear and tied to energy access and reliability, but is not distinctive versus peer utilities [6]. Community Impact (1/2): The company publishes sustainability reporting, has a net-zero 2050 goal, and Sustainalytics rates its ESG risk management as strong (rank 155 of 648 utilities), but no distinctive dollar-quantified community program was found [6][8]. Employee Retention (1/2): Glassdoor shows a 4.3/5 rating across 213 reviews with strong pay and benefits, though reviewers flag slow promotions and change; no tenure or turnover data was found [7]. Insider Buying (1/2): FMP data shows 3 open-market purchases versus 9 sales in Q1 2026 and no purchases in Q2-Q4 2026 - roughly neutral, with no meaningful CEO buying [5].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored (dividend sleeve, 12 weight units, weighted sum 9.14). D/E of 84.7% scores 0.94 and forward P/E of 15.5 scores 1.0 [3]. ROE of 6.7% scores only 0.45 and revenue growth of -0.1% YoY scores 0.66 [3]. The 5yr revenue CAGR of 3.9% (FY2020 $11.35B to FY2025 $13.71B, derived from FMP income statements) scores 0.59, and the 16.8% profit margin scores 0.84 [4]. Dividend metrics: payout ratio of 72.8% (FMP TTM) scores 0.45; 28 consecutive years paid (2x weight) and 23 consecutive years of growth both score 1.0; the 5yr dividend CAGR of 3.6% (quarterly dividend $0.55 in 2021 to $0.6575 in 2026, split-adjusted, derived from FMP dividend history) scores 0.61 at 2x weight [4][5]. Average daily dollar volume of roughly $320M clears the liquidity floor easily.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Sempra's earnings come from regulated wires, pipes, and LNG terminals - physical, franchise-protected infrastructure that AI cannot substitute [1][6]. AI is a demand tailwind: data-center and large-load interconnection growth in ERCOT drives Oncor's rate base expansion, which supports the affirmed 7-9% long-term EPS growth rate [2]. The residual risk is indirect - affordability and regulatory pushback in California if AI-driven load growth raises rates. AI Opportunity (0/1): Although AI load growth benefits Oncor, Sempra does not disclose quantified revenue attributable to AI customers or AI products, so the tiebreaker point is not awarded.

infinite_game.summary: Sempra plays a long game in capital allocation - multi-decade utility franchises, a multi-year capital plan, and 23 years of dividend growth - and has repeatedly reshaped its portfolio, from selling South American utilities to buying Oncor to selling a 45% stake in its infrastructure arm to KKR. Through Sinek's lens, however, its purpose reads as a utility mission rather than a Just Cause, its culture is solid but bureaucratic per employees, and its competitive language is largely regulatory and financial.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Sempra frames its purpose around delivering safe, reliable, affordable energy to roughly 40 million consumers and building modern energy networks, and its capital plan and net-zero 2050 commitment trace back to that purpose [6]. It is genuine and consequential, but it remains a utility service mission rather than an idealistic vision people sacrifice for.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): A 4.3/5 Glassdoor rating with strong pay and benefits indicates a stable, well-treated workforce [7]. Reviewers also describe slow promotion, management inconsistency, and a culture where 'change can be slow' - adequate trust, not exceptional empowerment [7].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): As a regulated monopoly operator, Sempra's public commentary centers on rate cases, capital plans, and EPS guidance rather than learning from named rivals [2]. No evidence was found of management framing competitors as benchmarks that sharpen its own performance.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): Sempra has fundamentally reshaped itself more than once - exiting South American utilities, acquiring a majority of Oncor to become a Texas growth story, and now selling 45% of Sempra Infrastructure Partners to KKR to refocus on regulated utilities [2]. These are deliberate, identity-changing portfolio pivots rather than incremental adjustments.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management has committed to a large multi-year capital program and long-dated LNG development while affirming 2026-2027 guidance [2]. However, funding growth partly through asset sales and a 72.8% payout ratio reflects balancing near-term EPS commitments more than sacrificing them for long-term capability [4].

investment_thesis: Sempra offers regulated-utility durability with above-average growth: management affirmed 2026 adjusted EPS of $4.80-$5.30, 2027 EPS of $5.10-$5.70, and a 7-9% long-term EPS growth rate, and Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.16 beat the $1.01 consensus [2][3]. Oncor gives Sempra direct exposure to ERCOT's data-center and electrification load growth, while SDG&E and SoCalGas provide monopoly franchises in Southern California [1][6]. At $86.06, the stock trades at 15.5x forward earnings with a 3.0% yield, 28 years of uninterrupted dividends, and 23 consecutive years of increases [3][5]. The pending sale of a 45% stake in Sempra Infrastructure Partners to KKR should simplify the story toward regulated earnings and fund capital needs without heavy equity issuance [2].
thesis_continued: The bear case starts with fundamentals that lag the narrative: revenue is flat (-0.1% YoY), Q2 2026 revenue of $3.0B missed consensus, ROE is just 6.7%, and FMP shows negative TTM free cash flow (-$8.02/share) as capex of $16.30/share runs at roughly twice operating cash flow [3][4]. Interest coverage of 2.4x and a 72.8% payout ratio leave limited cushion if rates stay high or regulators push back on affordability [4]. California wildfire liability and rate-case risk remain persistent overhangs, the KKR transaction still requires approvals, and LNG projects such as Port Arthur carry construction and cost risk [2]. The Inspire Impact score of -49 (MISALIGNED) is a display-only consideration for faith-aligned investors.
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 earnings on November 5, 2026, including any update to 2026-2027 EPS guidance and the 7-9% long-term growth rate
Closing of the 45% Sempra Infrastructure Partners stake sale to KKR, recycling capital into regulated rate base growth
Oncor large-load interconnections from ERCOT data centers driving rate base expansion and supporting a 24th consecutive dividend increase
key_risks: Negative free cash flow (capex ~2x operating cash flow) and 2.4x interest coverage require ongoing external financing; higher rates would compress returns
California wildfire liability, rate-case outcomes, and affordability politics could impair SDG&E and SoCalGas earnings
Execution risk on the KKR transaction and LNG development (Port Arthur), including approvals, cost overruns, and global LNG demand shifts
